C-TITLEBAR-MODE-CHIPS.Name: Titlebar mode chips: active-mode indicators with a two-group switch menu, per-mode hints, six new chrome glyphs
C-TITLEBAR-MODE-CHIPS.Summary: Non-standard editor modes are invisible and hard to leave. Split View, Source Code Mode, Diff Mode, Typewriter and Focus have no on-surface state: the View menu items are plain (no checkmark), all four exits (View menu toggle, ⌥⌘\, the tab context menu, the command palette) live off the surface the user stares at — the shortcut is exotic enough that the muscle-memory guess ⌘\ hits the sidebar toggle instead — and the split container itself has no close affordance (splitView.vue divider only drags and swaps). The owner hit exactly this on 2026-10-27 (owner quote: "bug — there is no way to figure out how to exit split view", originally in Russian) and chose the fix direction the same day (owner quote: "when any non-standard mode is on, show extra buttons on the titlebar with a menu that switches modes"). This change ships a titlebar chips cluster: in the standard state the bar is byte-identical to today (no wrapper rendered); when the current tab is in a non-standard mode, the right titlebar cluster grows mode chips — one document-view chip (icon + short label: Split / Source / Changes) for the exclusive view state of the current tab, and compact icon chips for the active writing modes (Typewriter, Focus; at most three chips total). Clicking any chip opens one menu of two groups — DOCUMENT VIEW (Standard / Split View / Source Code / Changes; exclusive: choosing another view exits the current one) and WRITING MODES (Typewriter / Focus; independent toggles) — plus a footer "Reset all modes" row. Every menu row carries a one-line hint and every chip the same hint as its tooltip (the owner could not say what Typewriter and Focus do — owner quote 2026-10-27: "I don't understand what the typewriter and focus modes are" — so the explanation must live in the product, not in chat). Six new glyphs join the frozen M-057 chromeIcons set on the same 16px/1.4-stroke grid. Repairs surfaced by the verification probe ride along: the e2e tauri-shim gains the missing __TAURI_EVENT_PLUGIN_INTERNALS__ mock, and view-modes.spec.ts is upgraded from shallow (class-presence / no-console-errors) to behavioral assertions (numeric focus opacity incl. headings; the typewriter stable-line invariant). When Split is active but collapsed below the 800px container floor, the chip stays visible with a narrow-window note in its tooltip so toggle state is never invisible.

Problem.Description: (1) Exit affordance: the split container has no close control — its divider only drags and swaps sides (splitView.vue:26-38); the menu item is a plain MenuItem, not a CheckMenuItem (m009_menu.rs:1189, vs the four check items at :1136-1165), so an active split shows no state and clicking the row again reads as "enable", not "exit"; the shortcut ⌥⌘\ is undiscoverable and the muscle-memory guess ⌘\ is taken by the in-editor sidebar toggle (the Cmd+\\ handler in editor.vue, corroborated by the in-file comment beside the view.split-view menu row in m009_menu.rs; anchor-cited — the tree is under active parallel edits and line numbers drift). (2) Owner comprehension: the writing modes were never explained anywhere in the product — the owner himself reported not understanding them (2026-10-27), which for users is fatal: the modes are dead weight without in-product teaching. (3) Shallow verification: view-modes.spec.ts asserts only that .ag-focus-mode appears (class presence) and that typewriter toggling throws no errors — nothing verifies the dimming values or the stable-line behaviour, so regressions in the actual mode mechanics would pass CI. (4) Harness gap found while verifying: clicking into document content triggers an @tauri-apps/api unlisten path that reads window.__TAURI_EVENT_PLUGIN_INTERNALS__ (node_modules/@tauri-apps/api/event.js:43); the e2e shim does not define it, so specs whose flow unregisters an IPC listener (the useIpcListener unmount path) inherit a pageerror that masks real signal — content-clicking flows reach it through that path, not on every click.

Goals.R-1: Surface and placement: a chips cluster in the titlebar right cluster. macOS: left of the theme button today; once C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES lands its quick-settings button, chips sit left of it (fixed order: chips → <> → theme → share). Windows/Linux: right cluster, before the caption buttons (theme stays the 4th caption cell, C-WINDOWS-TITLEBAR-ALIGNMENT). In the standard state (Standard view, no writing modes) no chip wrapper element is rendered at all — the bar's DOM is identical to today's.
Goals.R-2: Chip taxonomy: one document-view chip with icon + short label, reflecting the exclusive view state of the CURRENT tab (split / source / diff; reuses the existing per-tab flags tab.splitView, tab.diffMode and the source-code view state), swapping instantly on tab switch like the save-dot; compact icon-only chips for the global writing modes (typewriter, focus). At most three chips ever (1 view + 2 writing). The per-tab document lock is explicitly NOT a chip — its tab badge is the state indicator (C-40 T-004 precedent: per-tab non-view state does not get titlebar/menu chrome). Flag truth: the document-view chip reflects the VISIBLE surface, not raw flags, with the precedence diffMode > splitView > sourceCode — the code's own exclusion only hides split under diff while the tab's splitView flag can linger true, and split renders with a source pane whichever side the global sourceCode preference makes editable (that sub-behaviour is untouched). Menu view selections normalize the flags: Standard clears splitView, diffMode AND sourceCode; Split clears diffMode and sets splitView, leaving sourceCode to split's own editable-side rule; Source clears splitView and diffMode and sets sourceCode; Changes sets diffMode and clears the residual splitView flag. With no document open, no chips render at all — writing modes are global, but their indicator surface is the current document.
Goals.R-3: The switch menu: clicking any chip opens one popover menu (the existing titlebar popover/float patterns and neutral chrome styling, per the document-info popover precedent) with two groups. DOCUMENT VIEW — Standard / Split View / Source Code / Changes; exclusive semantics: selecting a different view exits the current one in the same action (no two-step "leave then enter"); the active view carries a checkmark. WRITING MODES — Typewriter / Focus as independent toggle rows with checkmarks. Footer row "Reset all modes": view → Standard, both writing modes off. Outside click closes; interactions inside the menu never close it; the menu is live — a mode toggled from any old surface (shortcut, native View menu, command palette) while the menu is open updates its rows and the chips immediately; shortcuts are shown where they exist (⌥⌘\, ⌘⌥S, ⌘D) and menu actions reuse the existing renderer command ids — no new command paths.
Goals.R-4: In-product explanations: every menu row carries a one-line hint under its label, and every chip carries the same hint as its tooltip; hints are new locale keys written as native copy in all ten locales. English reference copy: Standard — "the ordinary editor, text and formatting visible"; Split View — "source and rendered side by side"; Source Code — "edit the raw markdown"; Changes — "compare against the saved file"; Typewriter — "the cursor line stays at one height while the text scrolls"; Focus — "dims everything except the paragraph you are editing"; Reset all modes — "return to the standard view and turn writing modes off". Chip labels use SHORT forms (new keys: Split, Source, Changes, Typewriter, Focus); the native View menu keeps its full existing labels and is not touched. The complete new-key inventory is fifteen families: five short chip labels, seven row hints (the six mode hints plus the reset row's), the two group headers (Document View, Writing Modes), and the narrow-window note of R-7 — all ten static/locales/*.json gain all of them as native copy, and the .min.json twins are regenerated by the existing pipeline, never hand-edited. New-key presence and parity across the ten locales are pinned by a new unit suite at tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js (declared deliverable of this change).
Goals.R-5: Icons: six new glyphs join the frozen M-057 chromeIcons descriptor table on the shipped grid (0 0 16 16, shared 1.4 stroke, round caps/joins, currentColor): mode-standard (page with text lines), mode-split (two panes with a center divider — echo of the live split divider), mode-source (angle brackets), mode-diff (stacked plus/minus bars), mode-typewriter (a fixed line with up/down arrows either side), mode-focus (ring with center dot). Drawings are made on the .canvas/Icons.dc.html board per the set's LINKS convention; the chrome-icons unit tests pin the new names and the descriptor geometry contract; the glyphs must stay legible at the chips' render size (the plan fixes the px, in the titlebar-nav-btn family range).
Goals.R-6: Repairs shipped with this change: (a) tests/e2e/fixtures/tauri-shim.ts defines window.__TAURI_EVENT_PLUGIN_INTERNALS__ with a no-op unregisterListener (listen already flows through the mocked invoke) so content-clicking specs stop inheriting a synthetic pageerror — harness-only, no product behaviour change; (b) tests/e2e/view-modes.spec.ts is upgraded to behavioral assertions: focus mode — computed opacity of a non-active paragraph AND a heading is 0.25 while the active paragraph is 1, restored to 1 on toggle-off; typewriter mode — the active paragraph's center sits within tolerance of the fixed viewport line both right after activation and after a cursor move to the next paragraph (the stable-line invariant; probe-measured baseline: 477px before activation → 264px after → 264px after the move, on a 732px scroller).
Goals.R-7: Narrow-window honesty: when the current tab's split is active but the editor container is below MIN_SPLIT_WIDTH (800px, splitView.vue:58) and the layout has collapsed to a single pane, the Split chip remains rendered and its tooltip appends a narrow-window note (new locale key) so the mode's state is visible even while its layout is not. No layout behaviour changes — the collapse rule itself is untouched.
Goals.R-8: Governance: a new governed module M-062 owns the chips component and the switch menu (sources under src/renderer/src/components/titleBar/, verified by new unit tests and a dedicated e2e spec); a matching verification anchor V-M-062 owns this change's commands, scenarios and content-free log markers, both routed through the graph and verification indexes in the same bundle as the code; the dedicated e2e spec is tests/e2e/titlebar-mode-chips.spec.ts (named deliverable). The plan re-verifies M-062/V-M-062 are still free before claiming them (M-061/V-M-061 are reserved by C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES) and reconciles observed-write overlaps with the hot active tree (C-GITHUB-THEME, C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES, C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL and the uncommitted theme/editor work in the shared worktree) via grace lint --parallel-preflight before the first write.

Constraints.Item: No product code in this pass: this bundle adds spec.xml and design-context.xml only; plan.xml is a separate pass with its own owner approval. Implementation waves, corner matrix with verbatim Expected, and four-corner review passes (Correctness/Security/UX/Perf) belong to the plan.

No private or ephemeral absolute paths in committed artifacts: owner-side material (probe screenshots, chat originals, the ASCII mock cycle) is referenced by description only, never by machine-local paths — the C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES constraint bar.

Language: every committed artifact is English; owner quotes are translated with speaker and date; the Russian chat originals and the ASCII mock cycle stay owner-side material referenced by description only.
Exit is via the menu only — no × / close zone on the chips themselves (owner-accepted call, 2026-10-27): one interaction model, and the menu doubles as the switcher and the teacher.

No native View-menu CheckMenuItems for the per-tab modes (split / source / diff) — C-40 T-004's lock precedent stands: per-tab state is indicated where the tab is or on the chips surface, not in the app-global menu; mt_menu_set_checked and its allow-list are not extended by this change. Typewriter/Focus menu check state is out of scope for the same reason (their state is already visible as chips).

No mode-behaviour changes: STANDAR_Y stays 320 (the fixed line sitting above geometric center on tall windows is recorded as heritage behaviour, not a defect); focus opacity stays 0.25; the split 800px collapse rule and the diff/split mutual exclusion (v-show) are untouched.
No shortcuts are added, removed or rebound; the menu merely displays the existing ones.

Existing gates stay green and unweakened: npm test, renderer suites, e2e; grace lint --assertions current shows no new errors beyond the recorded pre-existing baseline; the shared-worktree parallel work is sequenced via grace lint --parallel-preflight re-run, not trusted, before the first write.

No release or train admission follows from approval: version bumps, tags and store uploads stay behind their separate owner release instruction. m048 build-mode notes: the titlebar chips surface is identical across desktop and MAS builds (the share button's shareCapable capability gate is the only existing per-channel difference in that cluster — its pathname condition is per-document, not per-channel — and neither is touched).

NonGoals.NonGoal: A close × on the chip; a hover-revealed exit zone; any second exit gesture beyond the menu (owner call recorded in Constraints).
Native View-menu checkmarks for split/source/diff/typewriter/focus, or extending the mt_menu_set_checked allow-list.
Changing what the modes do: STANDAR_Y, focus opacity, the 800px split collapse, diff/split exclusivity, lock behaviour — all untouched; the lock gets no chip.

Folding the modes into the C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES quick-settings panel (the "View tab" variant was proposed and rejected by the owner on 2026-10-27 — state must be visible without opening anything); likewise the single always-present modes button variant (rejected: it hides which mode is on).
New modes, mode persistence changes, per-mode preferences, or a modes section in Settings.
Mobile viewer surfaces; any mobile titlebar work.
Creating plan.xml in this pass; implementing any R-item; claiming M-062/V-M-062 in the live graph before the plan confirms availability.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Chips appear iff a mode is active: with the current tab in Standard view and no writing modes, the titlebar DOM contains no chip wrapper (identical to today); enabling split/source/diff shows exactly one document-view chip matching that tab's state; enabling typewriter/focus adds their compact chips; switching tabs swaps the view chip instantly; the lock never produces a chip.

Menu: opens from any chip; DOCUMENT VIEW rows are exclusive with a checkmark on the active view and a single-click switch that exits the current view; WRITING MODES rows toggle independently; "Reset all modes" returns Standard + both writing modes off; outside click closes, inside interactions do not; displayed shortcuts match the shipped bindings.

Hints and locales: every menu row shows its one-line hint and every chip's tooltip carries the same text; the complete fifteen-family key inventory (short chip labels, hints, group headers, reset row, narrow-window note) exists in all ten static/locales/*.json as native copy (product names and ⌘/⌥ notation untranslated); tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js pins presence and parity.

Flag truth and edges: with diff on and split still flagged, the chip shows Changes and the next menu view switch normalizes the stale splitView flag; split+source shows the Split chip with source's editable-side behaviour intact; with no document open no chips render; the open menu and chips update live when a mode is toggled from any old surface.

Icons: six new descriptors (mode-standard, mode-split, mode-source, mode-diff, mode-typewriter, mode-focus) render on the shared 16px/1.4-stroke grid with currentColor; chrome-icons unit tests pin the names and geometry; no existing glyph is renamed or redrawn.

Repairs: the shim defines __TAURI_EVENT_PLUGIN_INTERNALS__ and a content-clicking e2e run records zero pageerrors; view-modes.spec.ts asserts focus opacities numerically (non-active paragraph and heading 0.25, active 1, restored 1) and the typewriter stable-line invariant (active center near the fixed line after activation AND after a cursor move).

Narrow window: with split active and the container below 800px, the Split chip stays rendered and its tooltip includes the narrow-window note; collapsing/expanding never removes the chip while tab.splitView is true.

Governance: M-062/V-M-062 routed in the same bundle as the code with content-free markers; MODULE_CONTRACT/MODULE_MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY updated in touched files; npm test and grace lint clean against the recorded pre-existing baseline.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: npx vitest run tests/renderer/components/titleBar-deep.test.js tests/renderer/components/chrome-icons.test.js tests/renderer/i18n/locale-keys.test.js; npx playwright test tests/e2e/view-modes.spec.ts tests/e2e/titlebar-mode-chips.spec.ts --project=chromium; npm test; grace lint --path . --assertions current
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Unit: chip render matrix (mode × tab-state × standard-empty DOM), menu group semantics, descriptor-table pins, locale key presence across ten locales. E2E: chips visibility follows bus/command toggles; menu switch exits split in one click; focus opacity numbers and the typewriter stable-line invariant in the run log; zero pageerrors on content-clicking runs after the shim repair. Gates: npm test green, grace lint shows no new errors beyond the recorded baseline. Content-free markers: [TitleBar][mode-chips][BLOCK_CHIPS_RENDERED], [TitleBar][mode-chips][BLOCK_MENU_ACTION] with the command id.

Assumptions.Assumption: Owner decisions of 2026-10-27 are the design base, cited as decisions not proposals: the active-chips variant chosen over a single modes button and over folding into the quick-settings panel; hints live in the menu + tooltips; both writing modes stay in the product; exit via menu only; no lock chip. Original Russian quotes preserved owner-side; English translations with speaker/date appear in Summary and Problem.

Mode mechanics verified working by the 2026-10-27 probe (build current, Playwright + tauri-shim): typewriter moves the active paragraph from 477px to 264px from the scroller top and holds 264px across a cursor move (scroller 732px; STANDAR_Y target 320px, paragraph center lands at 264); focus sets non-active paragraphs and headings to computed opacity 0.25 with the active at 1, fully restored on toggle-off. The pageerror observed during probing is shim-only (missing __TAURI_EVENT_PLUGIN_INTERNALS__, present in real Tauri 2.6+ hosts). Probe screenshots and numbers are recorded in design-context.xml as the behavioural baseline.

M-062/V-M-062 are free at plan time: the runtime graph/verification documents end at M-059/V-M-059 (routed feature/governance documents reserve higher ids such as M-064/M-065 and V-M-901+, and C-LARGE-DOC-STAGE-0 reserves M-060/V-M-060), M-061/V-M-061 are reserved by the approved but unbuilt C-PAGE-WIDTH-TABLES, and M-062/V-M-062 appear in no index or active/archive change — the plan re-verifies before claiming; chips placement ordering rule is fixed for both landing orders of that change.
The ASCII mock cycle of 2026-10-27 (bar states, two-group menu, three layout variants with trade-offs) is owner-side working material; this spec's R-1/R-3 capture its chosen variant normatively.
